accounting_scope: For L=2B the bounded CUDA checker allocates 8*L*8 bytes: work 3L, inverse spectrum 3L, forward and inverse twiddles L each. All 8L words are copied H2D and 3L words D2H, including the discarded upper half; only B coefficients per component are compared. There are L native-extension pointwise products (6L base products), plus 3L inverse-normalization base products; FFT butterflies, twiddle setup, native numerator/denominator/Newton work and amplitude advances are additional. Host numerator, inverse, expected, two twiddle arrays and full result coexist with device data, plus vector/runtime overhead. No complete peak, canonical cap/setup reuse, live whole-PCS CUDA adapter, source-uniform work, rate, GPU time, real Gamma, new Lean lemma or H100 preflight credit. Existing PowerBlocks cap256 and State guard16 remain; the fixture has a stricter cap128. No wire/MAC representation, protocol, mask, exposure or transcript change.

scope: The existing PowerBlocks numerator construction is extracted without changing its arithmetic. Twelve fixtures export actual native numerator coefficients, inverse spectra and results for three consecutive blocks at B=2/8/32/128, independently compared to direct power sums. The C++ boundary preserves native Plonky3 E coordinates in Fp[v]/(v^3-v-1), not the wire/MAC u^3=2 representation. A six-base-product pointwise multiplication sits between three component forward FFTs and normalized inverse FFTs. The shared canonical parser rejects malformed/basis-mismatched/truncated/trailing/noncanonical/oversized/negative inputs; changed numerator, active inverse frequency and expected output fail. The matching CUDA consumer uses the same FFT launches and one additional product kernel, statically compiled but not executed. Adaptive, WHIR, ideal-streaming and real-Seed6 owner integration remain covered.
